complexity.notes: Correct but unidiomatic: the standard two-pointer solution tracks left/right maxima and accumulates water in O(1) per step for O(n) total with O(1) space, avoiding both the inner fill loop and the O(n) water array. The fill-on-record trick is what degrades this to quadratic on adversarial inputs like [1,2,3,...,n].
complexity.summary: A two-pointer scan from both ends that, every time the running water level (min of the two endpoint heights) reaches a new high, rewrites the whole current window of a water-level array; the answer is then summed as water[i] - height[i]. Each new record level triggers an O(n) fill, and there can be O(n) records (e.g. monotonically increasing heights), giving O(n^2) worst case; on random input records number ~log n, giving ~O(n log n).
